title: Before you integrate: what's the symmetry?
intro: Every integral below runs over symmetric bounds [-a, a]. Sort each by what its parity lets you do.

cards.text: The roll moment across a symmetric delta wing
Net AC voltage over one full cycle
The lift distribution across that same symmetric delta wing
Power dissipation over one AC cycle — which is why the device gets hot

debrief:
The wing and the AC cycle each appear twice on purpose. **Same bounds, same physical object, opposite verdicts** — because parity is a property of the integrand, not of the geometry. Lift is even across a symmetric wing and accumulates into the number you care about; roll moment is odd and cancels to exactly zero, which is *why* a symmetric wing doesn't roll on its own. Net AC voltage is odd and vanishes over a cycle; dissipated power is even and piles up, which is the entire reason a component with zero average voltage still needs a heatsink.

The two 'neither' cards are worth a second look. `x² + x` is a sum of an even and an odd part — you can still split it and kill the odd half, which is the shortcut in a more useful form. `eˣ` has no symmetry to exploit at all; it is neither even nor odd, despite looking tidy.

The habit is cheap: the parity test is O(1) and runs before an O(N) computation. Checking costs one substitution of -x. Not checking costs a full numerical integration to arrive at zero.
